name: Two pointers (fill from the end)
space: O(n) for the result, O(1) extra
whenToUse: Always for this problem: one pass over nums, no sort needed.

card.signals: "sorted in non-decreasing order" with negative values allowed: the squares are large at both ends and small in the middle. So the largest square is always at one of the two ends.
card.pattern: two pointers moving towards each other. left starts at the most negative value, right at the most positive value. A third index, write, fills result from the back. O(n) time.
card.coreIdea: compare the squares at left and right. Put the larger one into result[write], move that pointer one step inwards, and move write one step left. When left passes right, every value is placed.

invariant: Slots after write hold the largest squares, in their final order. Every value between left and right is still waiting, and its square is not larger than any placed square.

legend.text: left: most negative value not used yet; write: next slot to fill in result
right: most positive value not used yet
the value with the larger square
